seoTitle: Get Paid Daily, Weekly, or Monthly on eBay
metaDescription: Learn how to set up your eBay payout schedule so earnings from Managed Payments land in your bank account daily, weekly, or monthly.
intro: How often eBay actually pays you is a setting most sellers never touch, sitting quietly on the default schedule since the day they opened their account. Under eBay's Managed Payments system, you can switch between daily, biweekly, weekly, or monthly payouts, and the choice has a real effect on cash flow whether you're running a side account or a full store. This guide covers exactly where the setting lives, what each option actually changes, and the one tradeoff eBay itself flags before you save your choice.

steps.heading: Open Payments from Seller Hub
steps.body: From Seller Hub, go to the Payments area, sometimes labeled 'Manage payments and taxes.' This is the hub for everything related to how eBay pays you: payout method, payout schedule, tax documents like your Form 1099-K, and quick access to Tax invoices. If you've never been here before, note that this is separate from the Selling section you use to manage listings and orders — Payments is specifically about the money side.

steps.heading: Open the Payouts settings
steps.body: Inside the Payments area, look for the Payouts panel. It lists two settings side by side: Payout method, which controls where the money goes (your linked bank account or card), and Payout schedule, showing your current setting — in this example, Daily. Click into Payout schedule to change how often eBay sends funds.

image.caption: The Payouts panel inside eBay's Payments settings, showing Payout method and the current Payout schedule set to Daily.

steps.heading: Choose Daily, Weekly, Biweekly, or Monthly
steps.body: The Payout schedule screen lists four recurring options: Monthly (first Tuesday of each month), Biweekly (every other Tuesday), Weekly (Tuesdays), and Daily. Selecting Daily comes with a specific note — choosing it disables your on-demand payouts, since the daily schedule already pushes funds out continuously rather than needing a manual pull. Pick a radio button and the choice takes effect on your next payout cycle once you save.

image.caption: The Payout schedule screen, with Daily selected and a note that it disables on-demand payouts.

steps.heading: Weigh the actual tradeoff before choosing Daily
steps.body: eBay flags this directly on the same screen under 'Did you know...': a longer payout schedule might give you more time to accrue available funds to cover selling costs. In practice, that means Daily gets cash into your account fastest, but it also means fees, refunds, and returns get deducted from a smaller, faster-moving balance rather than a larger cushion that a Weekly or Monthly schedule builds up. Sellers running tight on cash flow tend to prefer Daily; sellers who want to avoid a negative balance bounce sometimes prefer Weekly or Monthly instead.

steps.heading: Confirm your payout method is set correctly
steps.body: Payout schedule only matters if the destination is right, so check Payout method in the same Payouts panel and confirm your linked bank account is current and verified. If you need to switch banks or add a new account, use the 'Add cards and accounts' option visible in the broader Payments settings page rather than editing the schedule screen, since these are two separate settings that happen to sit next to each other.

steps.heading: Track pending payouts and processing times
steps.body: Once your schedule is set, funds for a sale typically become available for payout after the item is marked delivered or the buyer's return window closes, not the moment the sale happens. Check the Payments dashboard regularly for pending payouts and any payment holds, which can occur on new seller accounts or after certain buyer disputes — a hold will delay a payout even if your schedule says Daily, so don't assume a schedule change alone guarantees same-day money.

faq.question: How do I change how often I get paid on eBay?
faq.answer: Go to Seller Hub > Payments > Payouts > Payout schedule, and choose Daily, Weekly, Biweekly, or Monthly. The change applies from your next payout cycle after you save.

faq.question: Does choosing Daily payouts mean I lose on-demand payouts?
faq.answer: Yes. eBay's Payout schedule screen notes directly that selecting Daily disables on-demand payouts, since the daily schedule already sends funds continuously.

faq.question: How fast are funds processed after a sale?
faq.answer: Funds generally become available for payout after an item is confirmed delivered or a return window closes, then go out according to your chosen schedule — the sale date and the payout date are not the same thing.

faq.question: Can I track pending payouts?
faq.answer: Yes, the Payments dashboard in Seller Hub shows pending payouts and any active payment holds so you can monitor exactly what's coming and when.

faq.question: What can cause payment delays even on a Daily schedule?
faq.answer: Payment holds — which can happen on newer seller accounts or after certain buyer disputes — delay a payout regardless of schedule, so keep an eye on the Payments dashboard rather than assuming Daily guarantees same-day funds.
